title: Cognitive Biases in Negotiation
description: Automatic mental shortcuts that cause negotiators to misjudge value, hold too firm, or miss opportunities.

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Automatic mental shortcuts that cause negotiators to misjudge value, hold too firm, or miss opportunities.

sections.title: How Each Bias Actually Appears
content: Fixed-Pie Bias: Assuming any gain for them is a loss for you. You miss a trade where they want a longer contract and you want a lower monthly price.
Overconfidence: You reject a reasonable offer because you're certain your BATNA is stronger than it is.
Reactive Devaluation: They offer a concession, and you instantly devalue it just because it came from them ('If they're offering it, it must be bad for us').

sections.title: Protection Strategy
content: Ask yourself before closing: 'What if I'm wrong about one key assumption?'
Use a preparation checklist that forces you to identify potential integrative issues.
Actively consider the opposite: 'What if their offer is actually reasonable?'

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Your brain lies to you during negotiations. A checklist is your best defense.
